card.name: Goli
card.era: adopted by the Baoule c.1900-1910 (originally from the Wan people)
card.tagline: Day-long Baoule masquerade of four sacred mask pairs
card.profile: Goli is a day-long masquerade dance of the Baoule people of central Cote d'Ivoire, adopted from their Wan neighbours around 1900-1910. Per the Metropolitan Museum of Art and Wikipedia, two dancers wear four mask types in a fixed order: the disc-shaped kple kple, the horned animal helmet goli glin, the ram-horned kpan pre and the human-faced kpan. Masks appear in male/female pairs and embody bush spirits; the event, accompanied by drums and palm wine, is staged for the funerals of notables and for entertainment, and is believed to protect the village.
card.insight: Goli has become the dominant Baoule dance, gradually displacing older forms, and its kple kple disc mask is among the most recognised of all African mask forms (Metropolitan Museum of Art; Wikipedia).
